subject: How accurate cutting supports a better fit
hook: Good fit on site is decided at the saw, long before anyone picks up a drill.
ig:
Good fit on site is decided at the saw, long before anyone picks up a drill.

Here is how one accurate cut carries through every stage of a cabinet:

1. The cutting list is checked against the drawing first. Most fitting problems start life as a typo.
2. Panels are cut on a sliding table panel saw, so long cuts run straight from end to end.
3. The first panel's diagonals are measured. Equal diagonals mean square, and the batch follows.
4. ABS edge banding bonds flat to a square edge. A wandering cut leaves gaps and lifting corners.
5. Hinge cups and shelf-pin rows are drilled off the panel edge, so a true edge means holes in the right place.
6. Square panels make a square carcass. That is why doors hang level and the gaps stay even.

If you are a joiner, kitchen fitter or cabinet maker sending out panel cutting, this is the standard worth asking for.

DM us your cutting list and we will come back with a priced breakdown.
fb:
Ever had a cabinet go together slightly out of square, then spent the afternoon packing hinges to get the doors to line up? Nine times out of ten the problem started at the saw.

In our Hanley workshop, panels go through the same order every time: cutting list checked, cut on the sliding table panel saw, first panel checked for square, edged, drilled, then assembled. Each step uses the one before as its reference, so an accurate cut early on saves time at every stage after it.

We cut, edge and drill for trade customers across Stoke-on-Trent and Staffordshire, alongside building our own furniture. Send us a cutting list and we will come back with a priced breakdown.
